subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw accept a bounded internal provider-normalized schema cache, using https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78664 or a replacement, as the canonical fix for this issue?
rationale: The source-level repeated-normalization path is clear, but the permanent cache key, invalidation scope, and provider-hook ownership boundary require maintainer intent before automation should create competing work.

options.title: Refresh and land the cache PR
options.body: Use the existing proof-positive PR as the canonical fix after resolving conflicts and confirming provider/runtime owner acceptance of its cache dimensions.

options.title: Replace with a narrower cache
options.body: Open a smaller maintainer-sponsored replacement only if the existing branch is too stale or its cache surface is broader than maintainers want.

options.title: Defer pending live provider proof
options.body: Keep the issue open without landing the cache until maintainers require live Google/Gemini before-and-after evidence for the anti-abuse symptom.

recommendation.title: Refresh and land the cache PR
recommendation.body: Use the existing proof-positive PR as the canonical fix after resolving conflicts and confirming provider/runtime owner acceptance of its cache dimensions.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete landed the original provider-compatibility PR and is the clearest available routing owner from current history and PR discussion.
